approved: Human Services Amendment (Photographic Identification and Fraud Prevention) Bill 2019
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would add a photo to Medicare cards to stop other people using them fraudulently.
It would require proof of eligibility and identity before a card is issued, and create a new offence for fraudulent use.
The offence carries a penalty of up to two years in prison or 50 penalty units, and the main changes start the day after royal assent.
Requires Medicare cards to include a photograph and other card information.
Makes the minister verify a person's identity and eligibility before issuing a card.
Creates a criminal offence for using another person's Medicare card or impersonating a cardholder to get benefits.
People who hold or apply for Medicare cards, and anyone who might misuse them.
